title: Microsoft Teams: AI-powered insights on meeting quality in the Teams admin center
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and Microsoft's tenant notice, including rollout windows, access roles and excluded telemetry. The documented admin paths and Graph operation are supported; licensing and feature-specific controls are appropriately left unconfirmed.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans AI-powered meeting-quality insights in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: AI-powered insights in the Teams admin center that identify emerging patterns, highlight impacted users and locations, and surface likely causes with recommended actions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The notice says the feature does not alter how customer data is stored or processed.
claims.quote: This feature uses AI/machine learning to analyze historical meeting-quality data and surface insights to admins; it does not alter how customer data is stored or processed.

claims.claim: The notice names no separate prerequisites for the insights.
claims.quote: No configuration is required. Once available in your tenant, navigate to Teams admin center > Meetings > Meetings to start reviewing insights.

claims.claim: No new identity, permission or consent requirement is described for the insights.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams admin center intelligent meeting quality insights external participants obfuscated consent switch budget cap. Read MC1523077, meeting troubleshooting and Teams admin roles; no new feature-specific requirement found.

claims.claim: The notice describes administrators taking recommended actions, not the feature changing settings itself.
claims.quote: When an anomaly is detected, administrators will be able to: ... Take recommended actions based on the likely cause and severity of the issue.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn page for these specific insights was found as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "intelligent insights" "meeting"; "intelligent insights" "meeting quality" licensing disable PowerShell. Opened meeting troubleshooting, Teams admin roles and best practice dashboard; results describe other experiences.

claims.claim: Learn does not state how these insights treat external participants' identifiable information.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams admin center intelligent meeting quality insights external participants obfuscated consent switch budget cap. Read meeting troubleshooting: its obfuscation rule concerns meeting participants, not this new insights view.

claims.claim: General user role assignment is at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Users > select the user > Assigned roles > Add assignments.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Users. ... Search for and select the user getting the role assignment. ... Select Assigned roles from the side menu, then select Add assignments.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments creates a Microsoft Entra directory role assignment.
claims.quote: Create a role assignment for the directory provider: ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments

claims.claim: The cited Entra admin center instructions are written for a signed-in Privileged Role Administrator.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as a Privileged Role Administrator.

claims.claim: Privileged Role Administrator is the least-privileged supported built-in role for delegated Graph role assignment.
claims.quote: Privileged Role Administrator is the least privileged role supported for this operation.

claims.claim: Delegated Graph role assignment also supports a custom role granting the required permissions.
claims.quote: For delegated access using work or school accounts, the signed-in user must be assigned a supported Microsoft Entra role or a custom role that grants the permissions required for this operation.

claims.claim: Graph directory role assignment requires RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory for delegated work or school access and application access.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory ... Application | RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory

claims.claim: The existing best practice configurations dashboard is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Best practice configurations.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Best practice configurations.

claims.claim: No API or automation equivalent for the existing best practice configurations dashboard is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "best practice configurations" "API" PowerShell; "Teams" "best practice configurations" "Graph". Opened best practice dashboard and read Teams PowerShell managing-teams search excerpts; no dashboard API found.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: The existing best practice dashboard highlights locations not following Microsoft's recommended practices.
claims.quote: The dashboard highlights locations that don't follow Microsoft's recommended best practices.

claims.claim: The best practice dashboard evaluates monitored areas over seven days.
claims.quote: All monitored areas are evaluated over a period of seven days.

claims.claim: The existing best practice dashboard is not documented as a control over the new insights.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams admin center intelligent insights meeting quality licensing tenant switch PowerShell best practice configurations dashboard API. Read best practice dashboard and MC1523077; they describe separate views and no dashboard control over insights.

claims.claim: The cited existing troubleshooting experience concerns individual users and meetings rather than documenting the new location-level insights.
claims.quote: This article describes how to use the meeting troubleshooting experience in the Microsoft Teams admin center to diagnose and resolve meeting and call quality issues for individual users and meetings across your organization.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Existing meeting troubleshooting data is available for all Teams users regardless of licence type.
claims.quote: Meeting troubleshooting data (real-time granular and aggregate) is available for all Teams users regardless of license type.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The depth and retention period of existing troubleshooting telemetry vary by licence.
claims.quote: However, the depth and retention period of telemetry data varies by license.

claims.claim: Existing real-time telemetry is available for Teams Premium and Teams Rooms Pro users for seven days after the meeting ends.
claims.quote: Real-time telemetry is available for users and accounts with Teams Premium and Teams Rooms Pro licenses for seven days after the meeting ends.

claims.claim: Existing aggregated meeting telemetry is available for all users for 30 days after the meeting ends.
claims.quote: Aggregated telemetry is available for all users for 30 days after the meeting ends.

claims.claim: The existing meeting troubleshooting experience obfuscates identifiable information for federated and external participants.
claims.quote: For federated and external participants, end-user identifiable information (EUII) is obfuscated to protect privacy in accordance with Microsoft data handling policies.

claims.claim: In existing peer-to-peer call troubleshooting, relevant identifiable information is not obfuscated.
claims.quote: For peer-to-peer (P2P) calls, relevant EUII is not obfuscated because the shared call session requires participant information to support effective troubleshooting.

claims.claim: Teams Communications Support Specialist uses basic troubleshooting tools and can only view user information for the specific user being searched for.
claims.quote: Troubleshoot communications issues within Teams by using basic tools. ... Access user profile page for troubleshooting calls in Call Analytics. Can only view user information for the specific user being searched for.

claims.claim: Teams admin roles can be scoped to selected users or groups using administrative units.
claims.quote: For more information about scoping these admin roles to select users/ groups within your organization, see Administrative units for Microsoft Teams

claims.claim: For existing meeting troubleshooting, an administrator's administrative unit assignment determines which users' meetings they can access.
claims.quote: If your organization uses Administrative Units (AUs), your AU assignment determines which users' meetings you can access.

claims.claim: For existing troubleshooting, partner admins using GDAP need Teams Communications Support Specialist or Teams Communications Support Engineer in the customer tenant.
claims.quote: Partner admins using Granular Delegated Admin Privileges (GDAP) must be assigned the Teams Communications Support Specialist (TCSS) or Teams Communications Support Engineer (TCSE) role in the customer tenant.
